previousComments: All 14 fixed. Each behaviour fix has a test that fails with it reverted (both reviews' mutation probes): the read by name and the dropped per-record stop, the reader's de-duplication and the session-file join, the single definition of where the override comment stands (the continuation case now keeps it), the entry-write refusal recorded as sent back, the marker count taken at the recorder's first Dispatch call, the single shutdown-cut owner. The abandoned() throw has no test because its state cannot be reached ('timeout' is set only by arm, which decide calls after the reads).

keyFindings.description: A late first upload erases records reported as written, uncounted. An upload the client gives up (60 s deadline, unsettled keyed window, or the shutdown cut) can still be running in Dispatch; the next record reads the name, gets 404, uploads under a new key and reports success, later records append, then the late upload commits and Dispatch replaces the text (artifacts.go:516). Records 2.. are gone with no recordError, record 1 is in Dispatch and counted lost. Both reviews reproduced it against the real recorder with a fake following Dispatch's replace-on-upload rule; that Dispatch commits the given-up upload after the second is [INFERENCE]. Fix: make creating a session's document one intent across attempts and processes (an Idempotency-Key derived from project and document name, which the client must accept from its caller), and correct :321-323, :343-345, README.md:619-623 and :636-639.

An unmarked write's tool_result now awaits its record with no bound, queued behind the session's gate records: against a Dispatch that never answers, the second record answered at 120 s (reproduced with the real client). The host times the handler out at 30 s, stalling the agent each time, and the advisor-gate entry, the only local count if the record is lost, is not written meanwhile, so a session killed in that window loses the decision from both reports uncounted. Fix: append the unmarked entry first, start its record without awaiting it, and land a failure as an advisor-gate-record follow-up keyed on the entry's own id, as the gate does.

The join copies a gated call's advisor-gate-record loss onto every advisor-gate entry with that toolCallId, unmarked ones included (they take the id of whichever tool_result read the ledger line); one lost record counted 3 times in the quality review's probe. Fix: skip the join for outcome 'unmarked', which carry their own recordError.

'records lost: the decision never reached Dispatch' and the stated reconciliation are false for a write given up after it reached Dispatch (decision-record.ts:44-46 says such a write may land). Call the figure what it is: records the session could not confirm, an upper bound on what Dispatch lacks.

recordVerdict: Not yet: the slow-Dispatch, shutdown-with-records-queued, concurrent-session and resumed-session cases hold (20 of 20 landed at 150 ms per write; 5 queued records all cut and counted at 1,273 ms), but the late-upload case loses records uncounted and the unmarked path can lose a decision from both reports.
